---
title: "Robert Solow"
description: "MIT economist, 1987 Nobel laureate, and the man who named the productivity paradox (1924–2023)."
toc: false
---

**Robert Solow** (1924–2023) was an MIT economist and 1987 Nobel laureate, the architect of
modern growth theory. His growth accounting showed that most long-run growth comes not from
adding capital and labor but from technological progress — the "Solow residual," which
became total factor productivity (he called it "a measure of our ignorance"). He named the
productivity paradox in 1987 with a single line: *"You can see the computer age everywhere
but in the productivity statistics."* Precise and skeptical, he spent a career warning
against over-claiming what the models actually show.
